summary: Iteration 12: verified drive.callback scope-grant fix. New test file /app/backend/tests/test_iter12.py (4/4 passed): unit-tests the callback via monkeypatched google_auth_oauthlib.flow.Flow.fetch_token (no real Google). Covers (a) scope as space-delimited string containing https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive -> RedirectResponse 307 to FRONTEND_URL/?drive=connected and db.drive_credentials {_id:'shared'} has drive scope + connected_by=qa.tester@example.com; (b) scope as LIST -> same success; (c) scope='openid' only -> /?drive=scope and NO credential doc written; (d) real public endpoint GET /api/drive/callback?state=unknown&code=x -> 307 /?drive=error. Teardown removes db.drive_credentials{_id:'shared'} so the real user still sees Not connected. Regression: tests/test_iter11.py + tests/test_auth.py = 26/26 passed. Note: tests must run under -n 0 (serial) due to shared motor loop; parallel xdist with multiple event loops conflicts with motor's loop-bound client.
critical_code_review_comments: drive.callback correctly reads granted scopes from flow.oauth2session.token['scope'] (string OR list) rather than flow.credentials.scopes which is None when the Flow was created with scopes=None. SCOPES ⊆ granted check is right.
On missing scope the state has already been consumed by find_one_and_delete; user must restart the OAuth flow (acceptable one-shot semantics).
Stored credential 'scopes' now reflects what Google actually granted (incremental auth-safe).
seed_data_creation: Each unit test inserts a TEST_state_* doc into db.drive_states (consumed by callback via find_one_and_delete) and transiently writes db.drive_credentials{_id:'shared'}; autouse fixture deletes drive_credentials after every test. Verified post-run: db.drive_credentials is empty, no TEST_ drive_states remain.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iter12.py uses a single module-level asyncio event loop so motor's loop-bound AsyncIOMotorClient works across tests. Run with -n 0 (serial) when invoking only this file; the module-level pytest.ini -n 2 --dist loadscope still works because the whole file pins to one worker. Full Google OAuth cannot be automated end-to-end; the monkeypatch pattern (Flow.fetch_token + Flow.credentials property) is the correct unit-test surface.
rca of the issue: Pre-fix: _flow(None) built Flow with scopes=None, so after fetch_token flow.credentials.scopes was None (derived from session.scope but not populated in all paths). The check `set(SCOPES).issubset(flow.credentials.scopes or [])` was always False -> /?drive=scope. Fix reads the raw OAuth token response flow.oauth2session.token['scope'] (which Google always returns per RFC 6749 §5.1 either as space-delimited string or list) and uses that for both the subset check and the persisted scopes column. Verified via monkeypatched Flow in all three branches (string-with-drive -> connected, list-with-drive -> connected, string-without-drive -> scope error).
